summary: Fail closed when a ticket writer checker is missing (issue534)

delivery.outcome: Resolve issue534 finding3: both hub and adopted commit/push hooks refuse ticket writes when neither managed nor hub writer-lease checker exists, preserving normal fencing and all non-ticket publication controls.
nonGoals: No parser, IR endpoint, seed-baseline, evidence-policy or other issue534 findings.
No source ownership transfer, lease-schema change, fixture-policy waiver, new deployment or standard release tag.
No change to legitimate managed/hub checker lookup, non-ticket target-push controls or independent review/merge.

architecture.decision: Make the existing checker-presence prerequisite explicit in the four maintained hook projections. Reuse real-Git writer fixtures in the current pre-push suite for commit/amend and push rejection, plus a real checker fallback control. No new permission or duplicated lease implementation. Full hosted CI exposed an existing four-digit allocation fixture that copied the hook without its checker. Include the actual managed checker/schema and explicit allocator-issued writer identity in that existing fixture; this is required positive coverage of the same missing-checker prerequisite, not a new objective or workstream.
architecture.rollback: Revert the material source change through the same governed independent publication route. Do not restore missing checker files or leases by hand in adopters.

validation.evidence: Real Git commit and amend attempts fail with the stable missing-checker diagnostic and preserve HEAD for hub and managed hook variants.
Real Git pushes fail and leave the bare remote unchanged when the checker has disappeared.
Actual valid writer/session and managed/hub fallback controls pass; existing unauthorized session, force-push and target branch checks remain enforced.
Canonical governance and native complete stack checks pass for current head/base before independent protected review and merge.
